options.title: BP Texas City: The Gauge Said the Tower Was Nearly Empty
options.first_line: At BP's Texas City refinery, the gauge says this tower is nearly empty.
options.first_frame: the refinery's tall steel tower in 3D cutaway against a grey sky, amber liquid already near its top, a green control-board readout beside it saying LOW, the date caption and the reconstruction tag

options.title: Texas City Refinery Explosion: Why Did This Stack Erupt?
options.first_line: At BP's Texas City refinery, flammable liquid is shooting out of the top of a vent stack.
options.first_frame: a tall rusted vent stack in 3D at the refinery, liquid spraying out of its top like a geyser and falling as mist, the date caption and the reconstruction tag

options.title: The Texas City Refinery Explosion: A Gauge That Couldn't See
options.first_line: BP's Texas City refinery is restarting a tower {fact3} feet tall, and its gauge can only see the bottom of it.
options.first_frame: the tall tower in 3D, a green bracket glowing on just its bottom few feet beside the level transmitter, the rest of the tower dark, the date caption and the reconstruction tag

why: The first frame shows a tower filling to the top while its gauge reads LOW, so even with the sound off a stranger is left asking how the gauge could be that wrong, and neither the title nor the first line answers it (C says the gauge only sees the bottom, which is the twist).
